title: Numbers Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Numbers chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Numbers Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Numbers Chapter 4.

questions.question: Who did the LORD speak to in Numbers 4:1?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:1 states that the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron.

questions.question: From which tribe were the sons of Kohath taken?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:2 says the sons of Kohath are from among the sons of Levi.

questions.question: What was the age range for those entering the work in the tabernacle?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:3 specifies the age from thirty years old and upward until fifty years old.

questions.question: What was the specific service of the sons of Kohath?
options: To care for the most holy things in the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: To care for the most holy things in the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:4 states that the service of the sons of Kohath was about the most holy things in the tabernacle.

questions.question: Who was responsible for taking down the covering vail when the camp set forward?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:5 says Aaron and his sons shall take down the covering vail when the camp setteth forward.

questions.question: What covering was put on the ark of testimony after the vail?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:6 says the covering of badgers' skins was put upon the ark of testimony after the vail.

questions.question: What color cloth was spread on the table of shewbread?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:7 states that a cloth of blue was spread upon the table of shewbread.

questions.question: True or False: The sons of Kohath were allowed to touch the holy things when bearing them.
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:15 warns that the sons of Kohath shall not touch any holy thing lest they die.

questions.question: Which of these items was not mentioned as being covered with badgers' skins?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:6-12 mention coverings for items like the ark, candlestick, and golden altar, but not the walls of the tabernacle.

questions.question: Who had oversight of the oil for the light, sweet incense, daily meat offering, and anointing oil?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:16 assigns these duties to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD commanded Moses and Aaron to cut off the tribe of Kohath from among the Levites.
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:18 specifically says, 'Cut ye not off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites.'

questions.question: What was spread on the altar after the ashes were taken away?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:13 states that after removing the ashes, a purple cloth was spread on the altar.

questions.question: True or False: The sons of Kohath were allowed to go in to see when the holy things were covered.
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:20 says they shall not go in to see when the holy things are covered, lest they die.

questions.question: In what order did the covering and carrying of the sanctuary take place according to Numbers 4:15?
options: Aaron and his sons cover the sanctuary, then the sons of Kohath bear it
Sons of Kohath cover the sanctuary, then Aaron and his sons bear it
Moses covers the sanctuary, then Aaron and his sons bear it
Sons of Gershon cover the sanctuary, then sons of Merari bear it
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron and his sons cover the sanctuary, then the sons of Kohath bear it
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:15 specifies that Aaron and his sons cover the sanctuary first, then the sons of Kohath come to bear it.

questions.question: What material was commonly used to cover holy items after the cloths?
questions.explanation: Multiple verses (e.g., Numbers 4:6, 4:8, 4:10) mention covering items with badgers' skins after cloth coverings.

medium.title: Numbers Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Numbers Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Numbers 4:18-20, what is the primary reason Aaron and his sons must appoint the sons of Kohath to their service and burden?
options: So they may live and not die when approaching the most holy things
To ensure the tabernacle is always clean
To organize the camp's daily meals
questions.correctAnswer: So they may live and not die when approaching the most holy things
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:18-20 explains that Aaron and his sons must appoint the Kohathites to their service so they may live and not die when approaching the most holy things, emphasizing the importance of proper handling of sacred duties.

questions.question: What does Numbers 4:22-23 specify about the age range of the sons of Gershon who are to be numbered for service?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:22-23 clearly states that the sons of Gershon to be numbered for service are those from thirty years old and upward until fifty years old, setting the specific age range for their duties.

questions.question: What specific items are the sons of Gershon tasked with carrying, according to Numbers 4:25-26?
options: The curtains of the tabernacle, coverings, hangings, cords, and all instruments of their service
The ark of the testimony and the golden altar
The table of shewbread and candlestick
The boards, bars, pillars, and sockets of the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: The curtains of the tabernacle, coverings, hangings, cords, and all instruments of their service
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:25-26 describes the Gershonites' charge as bearing the curtains, coverings, hangings of the court and gate, their cords, and all related instruments, differentiating their duties from those of other Levite families.

questions.question: Who is given charge over the service of the sons of Gershon, as stated in Numbers 4:28?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:28 assigns the charge of the Gershonites' service to Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest, highlighting the priestly oversight in their duties.

questions.question: According to Numbers 4:29-30, what is the age requirement for the sons of Merari to enter into service?
options: From 25 years old to 45 years old
From 30 years old to 50 years old
From 20 years old to 40 years old
From 35 years old to 55 years old
questions.correctAnswer: From 30 years old to 50 years old
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:29-30 specifies that the sons of Merari, like the other families of Levites, are to be numbered from thirty to fifty years old for service in the tabernacle.

questions.question: What specific parts of the tabernacle are the sons of Merari responsible for carrying, according to Numbers 4:31-32?
options: Boards, bars, pillars, sockets, pillars of the court, pins, cords, and all instruments
The ark, altar, table, and candlestick
The daily meat offering and anointing oil
questions.correctAnswer: Boards, bars, pillars, sockets, pillars of the court, pins, cords, and all instruments
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:31-32 outlines that the Merarites' charge includes carrying the structural components of the tabernacle such as boards, bars, pillars, sockets, pins, cords, and all related instruments.

questions.question: Under whose oversight are the sons of Merari placed for their service, as mentioned in Numbers 4:33?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:33 states that the service of the Merarites is under the hand of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest, indicating the priestly supervision of their duties.

questions.question: How many sons of Kohath were numbered from age thirty to fifty for service, according to Numbers 4:34-36?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:34-36 records that the numbered sons of Kohath who could do service from thirty to fifty years old were two thousand seven hundred and fifty.

questions.question: What is the total number of sons of Gershon counted for service from thirty to fifty years, as given in Numbers 4:38-40?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:38-40 states that the sons of Gershon numbered for service from thirty to fifty years old were two thousand six hundred and thirty.

questions.question: According to Numbers 4:42-44, how many sons of Merari were numbered for service from thirty to fifty years old?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:42-44 mentions that the sons of Merari numbered from thirty to fifty years old for service totaled three thousand two hundred.

questions.question: What is the total number of Levites counted for service from thirty to fifty years old as recorded in Numbers 4:46-48?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:46-48 sums the total Levites numbered for service from thirty to fifty years old as eight thousand five hundred and eighty.

questions.question: True or False: Numbers 4:19-20 teaches that the sons of Kohath should not look at the holy things when they are covered to avoid death.
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:19-20 instructs that the sons of Kohath shall not go in to see when the holy things are covered, lest they die, emphasizing reverence and obedience to God's commands.

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 4:27, the sons of Gershon perform their service independently without appointment from Aaron and his sons.
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:27 states that all the service of the sons of Gershon is at the appointment of Aaron and his sons, showing the importance of priestly oversight and order.

questions.question: True or False: Numbers 4:21-23 commands Moses to number the sons of Gershon from thirty to fifty years old for service in the tabernacle.
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:21-23 records the LORD's command to Moses to number the sons of Gershon from thirty years old and upward until fifty years old for service in the tabernacle, confirming the age range and duty.

questions.question: Based on Numbers 4:18-20 and 4:34-36, what practical lesson about leadership and obedience can believers learn from the handling of the holy things by the Kohathites?
options: Proper delegation and adherence to God’s commands protect believers from harm
Physical strength is the most important factor in service
Only the eldest should perform sacred duties
questions.correctAnswer: Proper delegation and adherence to God’s commands protect believers from harm
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:18-20 emphasizes that Aaron and his sons must appoint the Kohathites to their duties to ensure their safety when handling holy things, and Numbers 4:34-36 shows the careful numbering of those eligible, teaching that obedience and proper leadership are essential to faithful service and protection.

hard.title: Numbers Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Numbers Chapter 4.

questions.question: According to Numbers 4:36, how many sons of Kohath were numbered for service in the tabernacle?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:36 states that the numbered sons of Kohath were 2,750 for service in the tabernacle.

questions.question: What age range was required for Levites to enter service in the tabernacle according to Numbers 4:35?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:35 specifies the age range for service as from thirty years old and upward even unto fifty years old.

questions.question: How many sons of Gershon were numbered for service in the tabernacle according to Numbers 4:40?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:40 indicates that 2,630 sons of Gershon were counted for service in the tabernacle.

questions.question: What was the specific charge of the sons of Merari in the tabernacle, as described in Numbers 4:31?
options: Taking care of the holy vessels
Handling the boards, bars, pillars, and sockets of the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: Handling the boards, bars, pillars, and sockets of the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:31 outlines the charge of the sons of Merari as the boards, bars, pillars, sockets, and related items of the tabernacle.

questions.question: Who had oversight of the oil for the light, sweet incense, daily meat offering, and the anointing oil according to Numbers 4:16?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:16 assigns Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, the oversight of the oil for the light, sweet incense, daily meat offering, and anointing oil.

questions.question: According to Numbers 4:49, by whose commandment were the Levites numbered for their service?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:49 clarifies that the numbering was done by Moses according to the commandment of the LORD.

questions.question: Which tribe was specifically instructed not to be cut off from among the Levites in Numbers 4?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:18 commands not to cut off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites from among the Levites.

questions.question: According to Numbers 4:15, who was responsible for covering the sanctuary and its vessels before the sons of Kohath bore them?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:15 states that Aaron and his sons covered the sanctuary and vessels, after which the sons of Kohath would bear them.

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 4:20, the sons of Kohath were allowed to look upon the holy things when they were covered.
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:20 explicitly says they shall not go in to see when the holy things are covered, lest they die.

questions.question: True or False: The total number of Levites aged 30 to 50, counted for service in the tabernacle, was 8,580 according to Numbers 4.
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:48 states the total number counted was 8,580 for the Levites aged 30 to 50 for tabernacle service.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage closely relates to the detailed duties of the Levites in Numbers 4 by outlining the roles of Levites during the wilderness tabernacle period?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 23 provides detailed information on the divisions and duties of the Levites, paralleling Numbers 4's tabernacle service descriptions.

questions.question: What Hebrew word meaning 'burden' or 'charge' is significant in describing the responsibilities of the Levites in Numbers 4?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Masa' (meaning burden or charge) is significant in Numbers 4, describing the carrying responsibilities of the Levites.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Numbers 4 to organize the service duties of the three Levitical families (Kohath, Gershon, Merari)?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4 uses parallelism by systematically listing the duties and numbering of each Levitical family in a balanced and repeated pattern.

questions.question: How does the detailed numbering of Levites in Numbers 4 foreshadow New Testament themes about priestly service?
options: It foreshadows the priesthood of all believers, as in 1 Peter 2:9.
It predicts the destruction of the temple in Acts.
It symbolizes the need for animal sacrifices in Hebrews.
It shows the division of tribes in Revelation.
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the priesthood of all believers, as in 1 Peter 2:9.
questions.explanation: The Levites’ specialized service foreshadows the New Testament teaching in 1 Peter 2:9 about a royal priesthood of all believers, highlighting dedicated service to God.

questions.question: According to Numbers 4:44, how many sons of Merari were numbered for service in the tabernacle?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:44 states the sons of Merari numbered for service were 3,200.

theological.title: Numbers Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Numbers Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Numbers 4:3, what was the age range for the sons of Kohath to enter into the work of the tabernacle?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:3 specifies that those who enter into the host to do the work in the tabernacle must be from thirty years old and upward even until fifty years old.

questions.question: What specific task were the sons of Kohath assigned concerning the most holy things, as described in Numbers 4:4?
options: To carry the curtains and hangings
To do the service about the most holy things in the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: To do the service about the most holy things in the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:4 states that the service of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation was specifically about the most holy things.

questions.question: According to Numbers 4:5-6, who was responsible for covering the ark of testimony and what materials were used?
options: The sons of Gershon; cloth of blue and scarlet
Aaron and his sons; covering vail, badgers' skins, and a cloth of blue
The sons of Merari; badgers' skins and purple cloth
Moses and Aaron; golden cloth and scarlet fabric
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron and his sons; covering vail, badgers' skins, and a cloth of blue
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:5-6 explains Aaron and his sons were to take down the covering vail, cover the ark with it, then put on the covering of badgers' skins and spread a cloth wholly of blue over it.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is emphasized by the instruction that the sons of Kohath must not touch any holy thing lest they die (Numbers 4:15)?
options: The doctrine of God's holiness and human sanctity
The doctrine of justification by faith
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's holiness and human sanctity
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:15 highlights God's holiness and the sanctity required when approaching holy objects, emphasizing that improper contact with the holy things results in death, illustrating the separation between God and sinful humanity (cf. Hebrews 12:29).

questions.question: In Numbers 4:16, what responsibilities were given to Eleazar son of Aaron?
options: Oversight of the sons of Gershon
Guarding the entrance of the tabernacle
Responsibility for the oil for the light, sweet incense, daily meat offering, anointing oil, and overall oversight of the tabernacle and its vessels
questions.correctAnswer: Responsibility for the oil for the light, sweet incense, daily meat offering, anointing oil, and overall oversight of the tabernacle and its vessels
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:16 assigns Eleazar the charge over the oil for the light, sweet incense, daily meat offering, anointing oil, and the supervision of the tabernacle and all within it.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about God's mercy and justice is evidenced by Numbers 4:18-20 regarding the tribe of Kohathites?
options: That God's justice requires strict punishment without mercy
That God's mercy allows the Kohathites to live if they follow proper procedures, demonstrating both divine justice and mercy
That the Kohathites are exempt from God's laws
That God's justice is arbitrary and without clear guidelines
questions.correctAnswer: That God's mercy allows the Kohathites to live if they follow proper procedures, demonstrating both divine justice and mercy
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:18-20 shows God instructs Moses and Aaron to treat the Kohathites so they may live when approaching holy things, balancing divine justice (the prohibition against improper contact) with mercy (allowing them to live if obedient).

questions.question: According to Numbers 4:22-23, what is the age qualification for the sons of Gershon to perform their service?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:22-23 clearly states that the sons of Gershon, like the Kohathites, were numbered from thirty years old and upward until fifty years old for service in the tabernacle.

questions.question: What is the significance of the sons of Gershon bearing the curtains and hangings of the tabernacle as described in Numbers 4:25-26 in the broader redemptive narrative?
options: It demonstrates the burden of sin carried by priests
It symbolizes the responsibility of preserving God's presence and holiness among His people
It represents the judgment of God on Israel
It foreshadows the building of the temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the responsibility of preserving God's presence and holiness among His people
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:25-26 assigns the Gershonites to bear the curtains and coverings, symbolizing their role in maintaining the separation and sacred space for God's presence, central to God's covenant relationship and holiness theme in redemptive history.

questions.question: How does the division of service among the sons of Kohath, Gershon, and Merari (Numbers 4:29-33) reflect the doctrine of order and holiness in worship?
options: It reflects a chaotic approach to worship without structure
It shows that all Levites had identical duties
It reveals God's ordained order and distinct roles to maintain holiness and proper worship
It indicates that only priests were responsible for carrying burdens
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals God's ordained order and distinct roles to maintain holiness and proper worship
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:29-33 describes the specific charges of the Merarites, distinct from Kohathites and Gershonites, illustrating the divine order and separation of duties to uphold holiness in worship (cf. 1 Corinthians 14:40).

questions.question: According to Numbers 4:34-37, how many sons of Kohath were numbered for service in the tabernacle?
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:36 records that the number of the sons of Kohath counted by Moses and Aaron was two thousand seven hundred and fifty for service in the tabernacle.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by the precise numbering of the Levites from thirty to fifty years old for service (Numbers 4:39-44)?
options: God's holiness in separating the sacred from the profane
God's sovereignty and orderliness in worship
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty and orderliness in worship
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:39-44 shows God’s sovereign ordering in designating specific ages and numbers to serve, underscoring His attribute of divine orderliness in worship and service.

questions.question: What combined theological insight about the sanctity of worship and the role of priestly authority is seen in Numbers 4:27 and Numbers 4:28?
options: The Levites serve independently without priestly oversight
The service and burdens of the Gershonites are under the charge of Ithamar, son of Aaron, demonstrating priestly authority in worship sanctification
Only Moses had authority over the Levites
The Gershonites were exempt from carrying burdens
questions.correctAnswer: The service and burdens of the Gershonites are under the charge of Ithamar, son of Aaron, demonstrating priestly authority in worship sanctification
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:27-28 assigns all Gershonite service and burdens under Ithamar, Aaron's son, reflecting the theological doctrine of priestly oversight as essential to maintaining sanctity in worship (cf. Hebrews 7:11).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the detailed numbering and age restrictions in Numbers 4 reflect mere human bureaucracy rather than divine instruction. What does Numbers 4:46-49 actually teach about the nature of this numbering?
options: That it was an arbitrary human decision
That it was a divine commandment by the LORD through Moses, emphasizing God’s concern for order and holiness in service
That it was a tradition without theological significance
That it was meant to exclude most Levites from service
questions.correctAnswer: That it was a divine commandment by the LORD through Moses, emphasizing God’s concern for order and holiness in service
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:46-49 clarifies that the numbering was done according to the LORD's commandment by Moses, showing the divine origin and theological importance of order and holiness in the tabernacle ministry (cf. Exodus 30:21).

questions.question: What does the prohibition in Numbers 4:20 that the Kohathites 'shall not go in to see when the holy things are covered, lest they die' reveal about God's nature?
options: God's holiness and the necessity of reverence and obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and the necessity of reverence and obedience
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:20 forbids the Kohathites from looking upon the holy things uncovered, under penalty of death, highlighting God's absolute holiness and the importance of reverence and obedience in approaching Him (cf. Isaiah 6:3).

questions.question: How does the detailed description of covering and carrying the tabernacle furnishings (Numbers 4:5-14) typologically foreshadow Christ’s work and the doctrine of atonement?
options: It foreshadows Christ as the ultimate priest who covers sin and bears the burden of the people
It typifies the need for ritual sacrifices only
It points to the temple as a physical building only
It has no connection to Christ or atonement
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ as the ultimate priest who covers sin and bears the burden of the people
questions.explanation: The careful covering and carrying of holy things in Numbers 4:5-14 typologically points to Christ who intercedes as the high priest, covering sin and bearing the burden of believers (cf. Hebrews 9:11-12).
